title: Quick check: JavaScript and TypeScript Project Configuration

questions.prompt: In the context of “JavaScript and TypeScript Project Configuration” and “JavaScript configuration”, For the Next.js 16 documentation snapshot used in this course, the minimum Node.js version documented by the official installation guide is
options: any Node.js version, because Next.js does not use a runtime.
questions.explanation: The official installation documentation checked for this course specifies Node.js 20.9 or later; verify the requirements for the version you install.

questions.prompt: While implementing “JavaScript and TypeScript Project Configuration”, Which command creates a JavaScript App Router starter using the standard CLI?
questions.explanation: The create-next-app CLI supports choosing JavaScript and the App Router; exact defaults/options may change by release.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “JavaScript and TypeScript Project Configuration”, Before diagnosing a setup failure, which evidence is most useful?
options: Check Node.js and package-manager versions, the terminal error, package scripts, and the project’s installed Next.js version.
Delete the lockfile and dependencies immediately without recording the error.
Change unrelated framework versions until the error disappears.
Assume every terminal failure is a browser cache problem.
questions.answer_key: Check Node.js and package-manager versions, the terminal error, package scripts, and the project’s installed Next.js version.
questions.explanation: Reproducible setup troubleshooting begins with versions and the actual error, not unrelated changes.
